name: TN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+10 partisan lean in a Republican-leaning Tennessee seat
Incumbent David Kustoff running with a large financial advantage ($3.0M on hand vs. $13K)
Democratic challenger Heidi Kuhn raised only ~$40K, indicating minimal campaign infrastructure
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~96%
model.rationale: Kustoff combines incumbency, a double-digit Republican district lean, and an overwhelming money advantage against a barely funded challenger, while markets price the race at roughly 96% Republican. The forecast sits near the safe-Republican threshold, slightly beyond the fundamentals-only estimate given the lopsided resources.
model.watch: A surge of outside spending against Kustoff or a major scandal would be the main route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Tennessee's 8th District leans Republican by about ten points, and incumbent David Kustoff is seeking another term with the advantages that status brings. He has raised over $2.2 million and holds roughly $3 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Heidi Kuhn has raised under $40,000 with about $13,000 available. Several independent candidates are on the ballot but show no meaningful fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and resources. Prediction markets give Kustoff about a 96% chance of winning. The combination of a Republican-leaning electorate, incumbency, and a vast financial gap points to a comfortable Kustoff victory.
